chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Dawud ibn Farqad who said: a man narrated to me from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Khudayb al-Bajali who said:

I was accompanying Ibn Abi Layla as his traveling companion until we came to Medina. While we were in the mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) entered. I said to Ibn Abi Layla, Shall we go to him? He said, And what shall we do in his presence? I said, We would ask him and converse with him. He said, Arise. So we arose and went to him. He asked me about myself and my family, then said: Who is this with you? I said, Ibn Abi Layla, the judge of the Muslims.

He said to him: Are you Ibn Abi Layla, the judge of the Muslims? He said, Yes. He (peace be upon him) said: You take the wealth of this one and give it to that one, and you execute, and you separate husband from wife, fearing no one in that? He said, Yes. He said: So by what do you judge? He said, By what has reached me from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and from Ali (peace be upon him), and from Abu Bakr and Umar. He said: Has it reached you from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: Verily Ali (peace be upon him) is the most judicious among you? He said, Yes.

He said: Then how do you judge by other than the judgment of Ali (peace be upon him) when this has reached you? So what will you say when they bring a land of silver and a sky of silver, then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) takes your hand and stands you before your Lord, saying: O Lord! This one judged by other than what I judged! He said: So the face of Ibn Abi Layla turned pale until it became like saffron. Then he said to me, Find yourself another traveling companion. By Allah, I shall never speak a single word to you from my own head, ever.

key_terms.أَقْضَاكُمْ: The most judicious/qualified judge among you; a superlative affirming Ali's supreme legal authority
key_terms.قَاضِي الْمُسْلِمِينَ: Judge of the Muslims; a formal judicial appointment under the caliphate
key_terms.قَضَاءُ عَلِيٍّ: The judgment/judicial practice of Ali; referring to the authoritative legal precedents of Imam Ali (AS)
key_terms.مُزَامِلاً: Traveling companion; in early Arabic, one who shares a mount or rides alongside another

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say to a Muslim judge who admitted knowing Ali was the most qualified judge?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a pivotal encounter in the Prophet's mosque in Medina between Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) and Ibn Abi Layla, a prominent judge in the Abbasid court. The Imam confronts him about his judicial practice, and when Ibn Abi Layla admits he judges by the opinions of multiple authorities including the first two caliphs, the Imam challenges him: he has already acknowledged that the Prophet himself declared Ali to be the most qualified judge among all companions, yet he disregards this supreme qualification. The Imam's vivid eschatological warning strikes Ibn Abi Layla so deeply that he turns pale as saffron and severs all contact with the narrator who brought him to this encounter.
